section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: The BlendTable module was introduced in RISC OS 4.31. It supplies facilities for merging paletted colours at arbitrary ratios. This is required for SpriteExtend to provide support for translucent sprite rendering.

swi-definition.name: BlendTable_GenerateTable
swi-definition.description: Generate a table of blended palette entries

entry.register-use:
Flags:
Source sprite is a pointer to a sprite, not a pointer to a name Destination sprite is a pointer to a sprite, not a pointer to a name Lock table after creation Reserved, must be 0
Source mode, or pointer to source sprite area
0, or pointer to source sprite/sprite name
Destination mode, or pointer to destination sprite area
0, or pointer to destination sprite/sprite name

Translucency factor (0-255): 0 for opaque sprites, 255 for transparent sprites; that is, increasing values reduce the opacity of source (or, in converse terms, increase the translucency of the source)
Pointer to buffer for table, or 0 to return size required (may be omitted if locking area)

exit.register-use: Size of buffer required (if R6 = 0 on entry), or size of buffer used (if R6 was a pointer on entry)
Preserved (if R0 bit 2 clear), or pointer to cached data buffer (if R0 bit 2 set)

use.p: This SWI is used to generate a table of 'blended' palette entries for SpriteExtend (and other clients). The tables generated will be the product of the sizes of the palettes in the source and destination. The terms 'source' and 'destination' merely refer to the palettes in use. The 'source' is the palette which is being overlaid on to the 'destination'. The palettes will be blended in the ratio <translucency factor>:(255-<translucency factor>).

By setting bit 2, it is possible to lock the area in BlendTable's workspace, preventing the cached copy from being flushed by other clients. This ensures that the space can be used until the area is unlocked. If bit 2 is set, then the value in R6 on entry will be ignored (that is, no user buffer is required) and space will be allocated by the BlendTable module. A pointer to the buffer will be returned in R6 on exit and the client may use this as it wishes until the next mode change or until the buffer is unlocked. The buffer should be treated as read only.

The palettes are laid out in the form destination by source. That is, given a source palette value (src) and a destination palette value (dst), for a destination palette of dstcols colours, the blended palette value - in the destination palette - is to be found at (dst*dstcols + src).

swi-definition.name: BlendTable_UnlockTable
